component-metadata.author: knimeuser
component-metadata.description:
Metanode for data lookup in selected columns of input table 2 (bottom input) using IDs from input table 1 (top input).
IDs column in input table 1 can contain multiple values, delimiter should be specified if this is the case. In such cases, the metanode returns list of values for individual IDs in each cell preserving the order including duplicates and missing values (both '?' and 'None'; returned as empty strings '') by default. The duplicates can be set to be removed (set of unique values will be returned instead of full list), as well the empty strings (missing values).
IDs in both tables should correspond to each other also in data type format from the KNIME perspective (e.g. String). That is why there is the following internal data type reformatting for both, top and bottom tables: 1) values are checked for being float and integer and are written as integer if both conditions are met for all values (i.e. the data type change is done per whole column only!) in the given table ID column (e.g. 2.0 (Double) value is returned as 2 (Integer)); numerical values in the string data type are not adjusted expecting these were adjusted prior the metanode run to be in line with another table (e.g. "2.0" (String) will not be changed) 2) IDs column data type is changed to string type prior the top and bottom table joinin step If not sure about the IDs compatibility between the two tables, check and prepare them before running the metanode (string data format is the most robust one).
Please note that the order of looked up values separated by the delimiter will not be the same as the order of IDs in the top table IDs column if you select to remove empty strings or remove duplicate values!
The metanode can return original input table 1 with additional columns or only input table 1 IDs column with additional columns with looked up values.
Name of the added columns can be modified using specified prefix/suffix.

in-ports.port:
input table containing IDs column with optionally multiple IDs per one row
output table will be based on this table (the same # rows)
input table with columns containing data to be looked up and column with unique, individual IDs - multiple IDs are not possible, one ID has to point to exactly one row in this table

out-ports.port: input table 1 supplemented by looked up columns; not used columns does not have to be retained if specified
